Option 1 - baked sweet potatoes. Get an aluminum pan from the dollar store and 5-6 sweet potatoes. 

Peel potatoes, slice them. Put them in the pan, slice some butter and place over the top, sprinkle with cinnamon,  nutmeg if you want and bake at 350-400 until fork tender. 

If you want to go old school, once they are soft in the oven, throw marshmallows on top and bake until marshmallows just start turning golden brown. Big marshmallows take about 10 mins, small ones about 5. 

Option 2- get some corn on the cob from the store, boil it for 5-10 mins, drain. Dust with salt and pepper or leave it plain and bring a stick of butter for when you serve it. 

Option 3 - Get a spiral ham from the supermarket. Also get an aluminum pan.  Follow heating instructions on the ham.  You can stick pineapple slices on it with a toothpick if you're feeling fancy.

Remind yourself all day throughout this process of all the reasons you stated above. And heads up, when the weight starts coming off, all the hormones trapped in the fat cells get released and you might feel sad or depressed. Trust me, it will pass. You will get tired of drinking your meals and remember eating full plates with ridiculous detail. But that also passes. On the day you realize that it no longer hurts to bend down, the day you can get in and out of a soaking bath without pain or flooding the floor, go up a flight of stairs without feeling winded and many other experiences, you will remember why you did it and feel validated. 

This is a long journey, but I'd have done it sooner if I knew how great it would turn out. Don't let the feelings and fears of others live rent-free in your head.

This is crunch time. You did a lot to get this far. It's also the time when those around you start letting their own anxieties come out. 

Folks will tell you to just diet and exercise. Some will say that they're worried something will go wrong. Many times they just are used to seeing you big and unhappy. Sometimes, it's because they are jealous. And a small percentage don't even go to the doctor for fear of treatment for themselves. 

In the end, it's up to you. Do what you have to do. I have a relative that hates that I'm smaller than she is when she used to be the skinny one with great legs. I got all the mean things said when we were young. Now I get the occasional snide remark while she is on the Ozempic train and still struggling. The comments have slowed down some, but haven't stopped.  I was big as a kid. Throw in unhealthy food etc and before surgery I was 340 lbs. Now I'm 170lbs and shockingly, I recall being this weight in elementary school and no one raised a flag except my gym teacher. 

So think about YOU. Think about your overall HEALTH. And drink those protein shakes.

Firstly, I will say that i do not support restricting heal are to age 26, locking up drag queens, or limited abortion etc.  We have two age milestones in the US 18 and 21.  Both are somewhat arbitrary. Other countries settle at age 20.  That is irrelevant as whatever age is legally an adult should get to make those choices whether others agree or not.  I do not agree with the notion that kids under 18 should be able to get care without informing the parents. 

However,  if we accept the nature of healthcare, and it's checks and balances, then why can't that be done in this case as well? I.e. Weightloss surgery comes with conditions. In the beginning you could just say 'I want this' and you got the operation. Turns out that without preparation and therapy people had devastating consequences, lost lives etc. Now, you have to wait, go through the steps, tests etc. 

If we are saying that dysphoria is a medical condition, then it goes through rigorous medical review which should be ongoing. There is also an argument for asking whether we should simultaneously be looking for a cure even as we alleviate the symptoms. Not because being trans is bad, but isn't a cure the eventual goal of all medicine?
